question: Why is a moment not considered anything at all?
premises: Therefore indeed we do not consider a moment as anything at all.
In an action-moment, or in one moment, many actions occur quickly.
inference: A moment has no fixed substantial duration because many actions can occur within it.
uncertainties: kriyākṣaṇe may mean either 'in the moment of action' or 'in an action-moment'.
plain_english: Therefore we do not regard even a moment as anything at all, since in one action-moment—or in a single moment—many actions occur quickly.
